Emily (Sales): Hey team — Acme demo cluster is intermittently getting 429s during the guided flow. They report token counts dropping unexpectedly (their UI shows quota go from 120k -> 0). Logs show bursts, but total token usage doesn't seem to match what their client says.
Sam (Eng): Can you paste a rfc log or the X-Request-IDs? Also which route/model are they calling?
Emily (Sales): route: /v1/generate-chat, model: redwood-open-7b, client sample id: demo-acme-001
Emily (Sales): sample log snippet from their side:
```
2025-06-14T15:02:31Z ERROR request_id=req_9a1b2 X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 tokens_used=345
2025-06-14T15:02:31Z WARN request_id=req_9a1c4 burst_window_ms=1000 token_bucket=evicted
2025-06-14T15:02:32Z INFO request_id=req_9a1d5 status=429
```
Jia (ML): Streaming vs non-streaming? If they stream and then abort repeatedly, KV cache eviction might not refund reserved tokens. Any client-side reconnects?
Emily (Sales): They do stream and the client often hits cancel then quickly re-open a new session — could that cause double counting?
Sam (Eng): Yep. Our billing counts tokens on server-side acceptance; if a stream handshake reserves tokens up-front then a fast abort could leave the reservation until the bucket window expires. Need to check per-route burst reserve and eviction policy.
Elliot (DevEx): Quick check — run the internal quota view for the tenant: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' 'https://console.redwood.internal/quotas?tenant=acme-demo'` should show per-route usage, reserved, and eviction events.
Dave (SRE): I pulled the tenant record. They have per-route cap 200k/day, global tenant cap 250k/day, burst window 1s with burst allowance 8k tokens. During the demo we saw a short spike up to ~45k tokens/min due to reconnect storms. That pushed remaining down to 0 and triggered fallback 429s.
Sam (Eng): Two mitigations: 1) reduce client reconnection frequency / debounce on the demo UI, 2) temporarily increase per-route burst allowance or daily cap while we stabilize.
Emily (Sales): Customer is asking for a temporary bump for the demo tomorrow morning. How much we can safely give?
Dave (SRE): I can bump per-route to 350k/day for 24h and increase burst allowance to 30k tokens for the route. Will monitor. Anyone object?
Jia (ML): Also recommend we enable soft-fallback to a lower-cost model during high burst to avoid 429s (can be a routing policy for demo tenant).
Elliot (DevEx): I can add a quick SDK-side debounce snippet to the customer repo: `if (lastActivity < 500ms) skipReconnect()` — reduces reconnect storms.
Emily (Sales): Perfect. Please escalate the temporary bump and add notes for the pricing team — they might want to track how often demos request bumps.
Dave (SRE): Done — bumped route acme-demo:per-route-day=350000, burst_allowance=30000; monitor window active. Ops bot recorded change: `opsbot: quota-change tenant=acme-demo by=dave-sre delta=+100000` :white_check_mark:
opsbot: alert cleared — per-route cap change processed (change_id=cq_789a)
Emily (Sales): Thanks all. I'll tell the customer we applied a temporary bump and asked devex to drop the reconnect debounce.
Sam (Eng): Follow-up: we'll add an eviction metric to the per-tenant dashboard (evicted_reservations) so sales can see when demo flows cause this.
Emily (Sales): Awesome. Reopen if 429s reappear. :thumbsup:
